title: Guardrails First: Engineering Member-Facing Health AI — Rashi Agrawal, Hinge Health
talk_summary: A practitioner's framework for shipping member-facing health AI at Hinge Health, arguing that deterministic code must sit above the model for irreversible decisions, that safety must be continuously monitored on live traffic rather than gated once, and that humans need explicit decision rules when architecture is insufficient.

takeaways.technique: Verify the judge before changing the agent
takeaways.what_they_do: When a continuous judge score drops, first ask whether the judge itself is wrong (over-calling) before touching the agent; fixing a judge prompt is legitimate maintenance, not cheating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The rule is always ask, is the judge right before changing the agent's response? Fixing a judge prompt is not cheating.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic code layer above the model for irreversible routing
takeaways.what_they_do: A code layer runs on every turn before the model and makes irreversible decisions (emergency escalation, intent routing to the right capability, identity checks); the model only handles the long tail.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Code runs first. Code makes the irreversible decisions. The model handles what's left.

takeaways.technique: Continuous judges on live traffic, not just pre-launch golden sets
takeaways.what_they_do: Automated multi-dimension judges score real production conversations continuously, supplemented by user feedback signals and random trace sampling with 100% sampling on high-stakes cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: What actually holds up in production is judges that continuously keep scoring real conversations as they happen. Not a saved golden data set.

takeaways.technique: Worst-case severity and revealed risk tolerance for triage
takeaways.what_they_do: Severity is set by the worst plausible outcome, not frequency; severity is decoupled from who owns the fix or team capacity; the launch bar is calibrated to what the org already ships, not stated policy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A bug that lightly annoys 100% of users is way less severe than one that could cause serious harm in 0.1% of cases.

takeaways.what_they_do: For safety-class issues, when unsure, hold and fix; for polish-class issues, when unsure, ship. The framework tells you which way to lean rather than deciding for you.
takeaways.evidence_quote: For safety bugs, when you're not sure, always hold and fix.

takeaways.technique: Architectural PHI/secret stripping at the pipeline boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: Strip sensitive data at ingestion before it reaches storage, so dashboards and dev environments never contain it; production and non-production have no pipes between them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The architecture version strips PHI at the pipeline boundary. At ingestion before it ever reaches the data lake.
